title: Star-forming region RCW 108 in Ara
caption: The star-forming region RCW 108 in Ara, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope
celestial: NGC 6188, NGC 6193, RCW 108 · constellation Ara · about 4000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Bright and dark nebulae spread across this wide-field view, with the star cluster NGC 6193 on the left. The subject is RCW 108, a molecular cloud that is being destroyed by intense ultraviolet radiation from heavy, hot stars in that neighboring cluster.

The complex belongs to Ara OB1, a star-forming association deep in the southern sky in the constellation Ara, the Altar. A molecular cloud is a cold, dense cloud of gas and dust where new stars can form. In RCW 108, radiation from stars that have already formed is eroding that raw material.

The picture was taken with the Wide Field Imager, a camera made from a mosaic of detectors that covers a large patch of sky at once. It combines 12 separate images. Through each filter, four frames were taken with the telescope shifted slightly between them, so that the gaps between the camera's eight detectors were filled in.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (33.04 x 31.58 arcminutes) and distance (4000 light years), the frame spans roughly 38 × 37 light-years. Its light set out about 4,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This visible-light composite comes from the Wide Field Imager on the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope. The B filter is shown in blue, V in green and hydrogen-alpha in red.
understand.eye: Long exposures build up light the eye cannot gather, so the faint nebulae here would be far too dim to see like this by eye.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: Each full frame records over 67 million pixels across a field 32 arcminutes square. Exposures lasted 300 seconds per frame through the hydrogen-alpha filter and 60 seconds in B and V. Very faint seams may show where frames were joined, and star colors are slightly misaligned at the far corners because air bends different colors of light by different amounts. East is to the left and north is at the top.
alt: A wide star field with bright and dark nebulae and a star cluster on the left.
